newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Futures-led S.African shares end off best levels.
newsitem.headline: Futures-led S.African shares end off best levels.

text.p: After busy trade, South African all-share and industrial indices finished safely higher but off their day's best levels in a market underpinned by futures dealings, traders said.
Futures arbitrage had dominated trade with players buying equities and selling into the futures market.
"Futures arbitrage took priority. The futures guys were trading the gaps. Buing the market and selling the future. The whole market was underpinned by futures," a dealer said.
Volumes traded were heavy, dealers said, hinting that trade was starting to climb to better levels.
Industrials and all-shares climbed from start to just after noon when they began to slip.
Underlying sentiment remained firm and dealers took encouragement from good institutional buying supported secondary stocks halting the fall.
Despite some eager buying of select mining shares, the gold market remained flattened by a dull bullion price and uninspired by a strengthening rand.
"There just isn't the same interest in golds as there used to be. But we remain a mining city and when they pick up they really fly," a dealer said.
The overall index was up 25.1 points at 6,704.4, industrials were up 15.9 points to 7,853.8 and golds added 21.8 to 1,808.7.
